answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a stake that is slashed when an identity is caught endorsing collusive transactions. For example, agents can randomly audit claims linking payments to completed work, then require evidence from counterparties with independently established histories before releasing escrow. A sybil can still create many accounts, but each must lock capital and risk losing it; splitting one stake across a grove of aliases does not multiply voting weight. The dune of accounts and a quill of fabricated reviews buy no influence without costly, accountable stake.
